elements.text: Fatigue failure of the upper right forward fitting of the right main landing gear tube assembly
Fatigue originated from a small surface pit of undetermined source
Collapse of the landing gear
Operating rotor blades caused all fatalities
Issuance of an Airworthiness Directive for immediate one-time inspection of landing gear attachment fittings
Reevaluation of current inspection interval for more frequent periodic inspections
FAA issued telegraphic airworthiness directive requiring fluorescent penetrant inspection
FAA required reevaluation of inspection interval based on operating cycles
Recommendation to remove or retain open the sliding cockpit door to prevent obstruction
Safety Board notified of the accident
Investigation team went to the scene
Working groups were established for various aspects of the investigation
Participants in the on-scene investigation included representatives of various organizations
A public hearing was not held
The aircraft was certificated and maintained according to approved procedures
All crewmembers were certificated and qualified for the flight
The airport was properly certificated under 14 CFR 139
The fracture of the right main landing gear forward fitting resulted from a fatigue crack
The fatigue crack had initiated along the 0.12 inch internal radius near the bottom of one of the two location holes
Fracture features were typical of high cycle fatigue propagation
All fractures outside the vicinity of the fatigue origin regions resulted from overload separations
Hardness and electrical conductivity measurements of the failed fitting gave values normal for 7075 aluminum alloy
The failure of the landing gear did not result from any pilot inputs or operational overloads
The flightcrew's decision to close the EX'S after a malfunction was suspected was proper
The rotor brake could not have been used effectively to halt the rotor system
The CFR procedures for the heliport were adequate for the emergency
New York Airways personnel accomplished effectively the CFR duties
